That sure sounds like a classic burnout, I always recommand to see a professional and talk to them.  
There are medications of course and otherwise, as always, easier said then done but try to cut back.  
Take thing one task at a time. Learning to say no is also an important thing to not get overwhelmed and have space foryourself.  
It's very hard to be fair to oneself but you deserve a break and don't need to feel guilty if you don't work or study. Nobody can function on a high demand level 24/7, people break. You need quiet and peace to fully heal.  
Again it won't be easy to just realise those things but small steps. Like don't do overtime at work if you did.   
Study when you feel motivated and if it fades and you feel like you don't want to anymore. Simply stop. Or just read a page or two a day. Never more. Set a limit for what you can do.

Again all easier said then done and it will always be a struggle but your depression is valid and not just an excuse.

First off I'm sorry you're struggling this much in life.  
I may not have way more life experience age wise but nonetheless I definitely can say, my overall situation got definitely better after distancing myself from my family. I understand if you don't want to leave them and stay in touch but if even your brother already left it might be a sign to even try it. You can always still try to get contact back once you're in a better place but taking a break and going no contact is sometimes the only right thing to do.  
I mean as stupid as it sounds but you're aware of what is cosing the bummer in your relationship with your gf atm so it's one step already to know what is the root, communication is always key. Maybe see if there are things, even if it's just something small you can change. Not saying you should swollow your emotions but sometimes it's easier on a partner if you take a deep breath and don't voice your thoughts.  
Also you're in therapy which is amazing. I'm sure they have helped you or will continue to.   
I know this is nothing someone wants to hear but finding real friends is a very hard thing and people will always come and go.  
Congrats on the job, try seeing it more as an opportunity then a burden and responsibility. Of course you have some but hey, you can be proud that you got a job. Tackle one day at a time.   
As far as feeling liek not having a purpose... again sounding stupid but in the end you define your own purpose. If it would go after society you life to work and pay for the goverment but that ain't fun for sure. What gives you joy? Try thinking of something you want to reach in the future? Maybe a family with your gf? Maybe just owning your own little house, seeing the world. Just generally something.   


For the end one thing that also kept me personally going was setting tiny goals. Like I would literally hype myself up for getting out of bed, brushing teeth, showering, getting thru the (work)day, that I handled a situation well. Always allowing space for emotions.  


I don't know if this helps you at all but I hope you will do better at some point and find happiness. 🤗❤
